title: Reading and Setting Form Values
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of reading and setting form values in a jQuery application.
Apply the .val() getter in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify setting input values with an explicit test or browser observation.
status_note: Draft generated from the attached syllabus and official references; requires lesson-by-lesson technical review, local execution, accessibility checks, and editorial approval.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through reading and setting form values with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns the .val() getter into a repeatable implementation choice. Attributes describe markup; properties represent current DOM state. For example, checked and selected are runtime properties, while data-* attributes are markup strings and jQuery data values are a separate cache.

task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates reading and setting form values using a current, documented approach.
The learner records the expected and actual behavior and checks at least one edge case.
The example preserves semantic HTML and does not render untrusted data as HTML.
The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
